704314.t: From ἐξίστημι (exístēmi, “to displace”) from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).

704320.t: From ἐκτείνω (ekteínō, “I stretch out”) + -σις (-sĭs), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) + τείνω (teínō, “I stretch”).

704376.t: From Proto-Hellenic *elaíwā (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀨𐀷 (e-ra-wa)). Probably a borrowing from a Mediterranean Pre-Greek source, which may also be the source of Old Armenian եւղ (ewł, “oil”).

704380.t: From Proto-Hellenic *élaiwon (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐁉𐀺 (e-ra3-wo)). See further ἐλαία (elaía, “olive”).

704388.t: From Proto-Hellenic *elə́t͏̌t͏̌ōs, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁léngʷʰ-yōs, from *h₁lengʷʰ- (“light (of weight)”). Synchronically ἐλαχύς (elakhús) + *-ϳων (*-jōn).

704339.t: From ἐκ (ek, “out”), formed on the model of ἐντός (entós, “within, inside”). Cognate with Old Irish acht (“but, provided that”), Gothic 𐌰𐌹𐌸𐌸𐌰𐌿 (aiþþau, “or, otherwise”).

704397.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁elh₂- (“to drive somewhere”), albeit with no certain cognates.

704399.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eləpʰrós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ln̥gʷʰrós (“lightweight”). See also ἐλαχύς (elăkhŭ́s, “small, short”).

704385.t: From ἐλαύνω (elaúnō, “to strike”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

704389.t: No certain etymology. Maybe from the same source of Proto-Germanic *linþaz (“pliable”) and Latin lentus (“flexible”).

704350.t: From ἐκτυπόω (ektŭpóō, “to model or work in relief”) + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

704315.t: ἐκ- (ek-, “out of, from”) + στρατεύω (străteúō, “to advance with an army; wage war; serve in an army”) from στρατός (strătós, “army, band of men”) + -εύω (-eúō, verbal suffix)

704396.t: From ἐλαττόω (elattóō), Attic variant of ἐλασσόω (elassóō, “to make smaller, lessen”), + -σις (-sis).

704391.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁l̥h₂-tós, verbal adjective of *h₁elh₂- (“to drive somewhere”). By surface analysis, ἐλα(ύνω) (ela(únō)) + -τός (-tós).
